claims.text: Rapid quenching by arc melting on a water-cooled Cu hearth stabilizes an fcc plus C14 Laves dual-phase microstructure in FeCoNiTi.
The fcc plus C14 dual-phase microstructure increases coercivity relative to a single-phase fcc alloy.
As-cast nominally equiatomic FeCoNiTi contains fcc and hexagonal C14 Laves phases.
Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29 is a C14-dominant variant.
The ferromagnetic fcc phase has an approximate composition of Fe21.3Co24.8Ni32.2Ti21.6.
The C14 Laves phase has an approximate composition of Fe27.3Co26.6Ni17.4Ti28.7.
The fcc phase is ferromagnetic.
Coexistence of the fcc and C14 phases enables domain-wall pinning.
The Fe, Co, and Ni sublattices couple antiferromagnetically to the Ti sublattice.
Antiferromagnetic sublattice coupling reduces the overall saturation magnetization.
Antiferromagnetic sublattice coupling enhances ferromagnetic ordering in the fcc phase.
The fcc phase has a magnetic ordering temperature of 1084 K.
The fcc orbital moment, the presence of the C14 phase, and interfacial spin canting contribute to increased coercivity.
The dual-phase alloy will have a coercive field near 667 Oe at 400 K.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni high-entropy alloys have coercive fields below 100 Oe.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni high-entropy alloys have limited orbital-moment contributions.
Magnetic transitions near 168 K and 1084 K are attributable to the fcc phase.
The coercivity enhancement requires coexistence of the fcc and C14 phases with the specified chemical segregation.
Neither a pure fcc phase nor a pure C14 phase will exhibit the same high coercivity as the dual-phase material.
Neither a pure fcc phase nor a pure C14 phase will exhibit the same multiple-transition behavior as the dual-phase material.

contradictions.description: The Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29 comparison alloy is called compositionally matched to nominally equiatomic FeCoNiTi, although its elemental proportions differ substantially.
Measurements are limited to 400 K, but the experiment is expected to identify or falsify a transition at 1084 K, which cannot be directly observed over the stated temperature range.

The experimental design prepares a C14-dominant comparison sample, whereas the predicted outcome and falsification rule require comparison against a single-phase fcc baseline that the design does not prepare.
